title: Service guarantees framing playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This playbook is a concise, negotiation-ready reference for GTM, sales engineering, and legal when positioning Redwood Dedicated/Private capacity to large platform customers. It focuses on the promise set we should own: predictable throughput, operational isolation, and legally defensible service guarantees that are procurement-friendly.

Quick elevator framing (2 lines):
- We guarantee predictable throughput and isolation for mission-critical inference with measurable SLOs and pragmatic remedies, so your product teams don’t have to build complex runtime routing or overprovision GPUs.
- We combine transparent unit economics + configurable fallbacks to keep apps online and costs bounded when demand spikes.

Buyer personas and what they care about:
- Platform Architect / Infra Lead: throughput determinism, burst controls, integration (VPC/KMS), telemetry hooks.
- Head of ML / ML Eng Manager: model parity, KV cache warmup, cold-start behavior, reproducibility across versions.
- Procurement / Legal: clear SLO definitions, remedies (credits, termination), data isolation language, auditability.
- Product / Feature Manager: availability for customer-facing features, latency percentiles, degradation behavior under overload.

Three-tier SLO ladder (sales-friendly):
- Bronze (economy): 99.0% successful request completion under committed QPS; 95th percentile latency target for generate endpoints; soft-fallback to lower-cost quantized model.
- Silver (standard): 99.5% completion; 95th percentile latency <= X ms (region-dependent); autoscale headroom + KV cache warmup guarantees; prioritized routing within region.
- Gold (mission critical): 99.9% completion; 99th percentile latency targets; dedicated isolated pool, reserved capacity for burst up to N% above commit; 24/7 escalation and SRE runbook.

Notes: keep numbers region- and model-specific in the contract appendix. Avoid absolute millisecond commitments in initial commercial decks; frame as percentile targets with hardware- and model-conditioned addendum.

Procurement-ready contract language (short snippets):
- SLO definition: "Successful request completion" = request processed end-to-end by a Redwood-managed model endpoint returning a non-5xx code and token stream within the latency window specified in Appendix A. Rack/instance-level failures that exceed 0.01% outside of planned maintenance are counted toward remedy calculations.
- Remedies: For any monthly period where Service Commitment is not met, Customer is eligible for Service Credits per Appendix B. Credits are the exclusive remedy except in cases of gross negligence or willful misconduct.
- Isolation clause: Customer’s Dedicated Capacity will be provisioned in logically and physically isolated compute pools with tenant-level encryption keys. Redwood will not co-locate unrelated third-party workloads in the same isolated pool without Customer consent.
- Fallback policy: Redwood may route overflow traffic to a compatible, lower-cost model variant (e.g., quantized or smaller architecture) after Customer is notified. Any output divergence risk must be accepted in writing.

Competitive positioning vs common alternatives (talking points):
- Public cloud managed endpoints (large cloud provider): they offer scale but not inference-aware caching or model-specific kernel tuning. Talking point: "We deliver consistent per-token economics and far lower tail latency for autoregressive workloads via KV-aware routing and continuous batching."
- Self-hosting/open-source runtimes: cheaper at peak but operational burden high. Talking point: "You can keep control of models without recruiting a 24/7 SRE team; we transfer the ops risk back to us with an SLA you can actually measure."
- Vendor X (closed model API): good latency but limited deployment modes. Talking point: "We give you both hosted speed and private/VPC options plus pricing transparency for audits and chargeback."

Deal-room assets to prep (checklist):
- Technical appendix: model performance matrix (latency, tokens/sec) by SKU and region.
- Appendix A: region & model conditioned SLO tables (to be attached to each quote).
- Appendix B: service credit tariff schedule (mapped to missed SLO windows).
- Runbooks: incident flow for capacity events and warmup protocol for cold KV caches.
- PoC plan: 2-week capacity test that measures 99th pctl latency and cache steady-state.

Negotiation playbook (sample script snippets):
- Procurement: "We understand you need an enforceable guarantee. Our SLOs are delivered with measurable telemetry and a simple credit remedy ladder. For higher assurance, we recommend Gold level with reserved burst headroom — we can model the cost tradeoff for you."
- Technical buyer pushback on credits: "Credits are narrow but designed to align incentives; we also include incident retros and SRE support windows for Gold customers. If you need operational change controls, we can add change-freeze windows to the contract."
- IRL escalation: always include a named SRE on the Gold contract PDF and a 2-hour on-call SLA for mitigation steps.

Objection handling (concise):
- "What if your model is wrong or lower quality after fallback?" -> "We limit fallbacks to compatible variants and require customer acknowledgment in Appendix C; we also provide version pinning and A/B rollout paths to control quality impact."
- "Why not just self-host?" -> "Self-hosting shifts full operational, security, and people costs to you; our numbers show effective cost-of-ops savings at 3–6 engineers for a mid-sized production inference footprint."
- "Can you prove it?" -> "We perform PoCs with telemetry and we can share anonymized benchmark traces under NDA; also see Appendix: sample 30-day throughput test results."

Short legal FAQs for our counsel (bullet answers):
- Indemnity: standard mutual indemnity with carveouts for third-party model IP misuse.
- Data residency: specify region by contract and offer Private deployment option for air-gapped needs.
- Audit rights: allow audit with notice and scope limited to SLA-relevant telemetry.

Operational runbook highlights for SRE/SE handoff:
- Pre-onboard checklist: ping-pong on QPS, 95/99 latencies, workload token distribution, warmup plan for KV cache, model version pins.
- Day 0–7: staged traffic ramp, monitor token-per-second and cache hit ratio, validate failover to fallback variant in canary.
- Post-onboard: monthly capacity review, quarterly SLO recalibration tied to real traffic histograms.

Pricing framing for sales decks (short):
- Present a per-unit committed QPS or tokens/month price, plus a small reserved-capacity uplift for Gold headroom.
- Offer a short-term trial discount for PoC testing months and lock-in credits on annual contracts.
- ROI line: show headcount avoided for ops + expected percent reduction in per-token cost vs naively overprovisioned self-hosting.

Open questions / TODOs (shared workspace items):
- Decide default latency windows to list in Bronze/Silver templates (region- and model-specific).
- Finalize Appendix B credit ladder numbers with Finance.
- Validate wording of fallback policy with Legal (explicit customer acknowledgment flow).
- Create contract-ready addendum templates for Private (air-gapped) customers.

Appendix (examples to copy into quotes):
- Sample billing note: "Committed capacity is billed monthly at the agreed SKU rate. Unused reserved capacity can be carried up to X% for Y months (see Appendix D). Overage is billed at the on-demand SKU rate."
- Sample SLA excerpt: "Customers on Gold plans shall receive a named SRE response within two hours of a Severity-1 capacity incident and a joint incident review within five business days."

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally pragmatic and contract-forward. Keep the language testable (telemetry keys, percentiles, windows). We want procurement to read this and trust that the SLOs are measurable and the remedies are narrow but meaningful.

Contact / follow-up: @maya.chen (owner) — drop questions in slack:#procurement-ops.
